artifact.reason: Existing safety monitor API. BrakeController integrates here. E-stop APIs already handle brake engagement.
Integration point for BRAKE_ON_ESTOP. E-stop already engages brakes via sr_emergency_disable_all().
CRITICAL: Brake control API already exists! sr_set_brake(axis, release) controls shift register brake bits.
Brake bit manipulation implementation. sr_emergency_disable_all() is ISR-safe.
Brake bit positions: SR_X_BRAKE=2, SR_Y_BRAKE=6, SR_Z_BRAKE=10, SR_A_BRAKE=14, SR_B_BRAKE=18. Active-low: 0=engaged, 1=released.
ALREADY DEFINED: TIMING_BRAKE_ENGAGE_MS=50, TIMING_BRAKE_RELEASE_MS=30, TIMING_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S=300. No need to add timing constants.
ALREADY DEFINED: CMD_BRAKE="BRAKE". EndSwitchMode enum pattern to follow for BrakeStrategy.
Modify en_handler for BRAKE_ON_DISABLE integration. Extend stat_handler for BRAKES: field.

interface.name: sr_set_brake
interface.notes: axis 0-6 (X-D have brakes, E has no brake). release=true releases brake, release=false engages. Updates shadow only - call sr_update() to latch.

interface.name: sr_update
interface.notes: Thread-safe. Latches shadow register to hardware outputs.

interface.name: sr_emergency_disable_all
interface.notes: ISR-safe. Sets OE HIGH, clears shadow to zeros (all brakes engaged), shifts zeros. Completes within 100us.

interface.name: safety_monitor_is_estop_active
interface.notes: Returns true if system is in E-stop mode.

interface.name: event_publish (proposed)
interface.notes: Use for EVENT BRAKE axis ENGAGED/RELEASED notifications.

constraints.constraint: Header-Only Configuration: Every configurable value MUST be in a header file. No magic numbers in source.
Dual-Core Separation: Core 0 handles communication and safety (safety_monitor_task at priority 24). Core 1 handles motion.
Active-Low Brake Logic: SR bit = 0 means brake ENGAGED (spring applied). SR bit = 1 means brake RELEASED (electromagnet powered).
Fail-Safe Design: Power loss causes all outputs to float LOW, engaging all brakes mechanically.
Brake Timing Critical: MUST engage brake BEFORE removing motor torque (TIMING_BRAKE_ENGAGE_MS delay). MUST wait TIMING_BRAKE_RELEASE_MS after enabling before releasing brake.
sr_emergency_disable_all() Already Handles Brakes: E-stop ISR already engages all brakes. BRAKE_ON_ESTOP should NOT duplicate this behavior on normal disable.
Stepper Axes Have No Brakes: C, D stepper axes have brake bits not connected to hardware. E-axis marked as having brake in SR but verify hardware.

tests.standards: ESP-IDF Unity test framework. Component-level unit tests in each component's test/ folder. Integration tests in firmware/test/integration/. Mock HAL dependencies for unit tests. Use TEST command for hardware-in-loop testing.

ideas.idea: Test BRAKE_ON_DISABLE: disable axis, verify brake engages before EN bit cleared (timing via mock/spy)
Test BRAKE_ON_ESTOP: disable axis normally, verify brake NOT engaged; then trigger E-stop, verify brake engaged
Test BRAKE_ON_IDLE: enable axis, wait idle timeout, verify brake engaged and EVENT published; send motion, verify brake released
Test BRAKE_MANUAL: verify BRAKE command works when strategy=MANUAL, rejected with ERR_BRAKE_AUTO otherwise
Test timing sequence with mock timers: engage delay before disable, release delay after enable
Test per-axis independence: Z=BRAKE_ON_DISABLE, X=BRAKE_ON_ESTOP, verify independent behavior
Test STAT includes BRAKES: field with correct format

implementationNotes.note: EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: sr_set_brake(), TIMING_BRAKE_ENGAGE_MS, TIMING_BRAKE_RELEASE_MS, CMD_BRAKE are ALREADY defined. Tasks 2 and 7 are partially complete.
BrakeStrategy Enum Location: Add to config_defaults.h following EndSwitchMode pattern in config_commands.h.
BRAKE_ON_IDLE Timer: Use esp_timer for per-axis idle timeout. Reset on MOVE, MOVR, VEL commands. Callback notifies BrakeController to engage.
EN Command Integration: Wrap existing en_handler logic. On disable: engage brake -> delay -> clear enable. On enable: set enable -> delay -> release brake.
E-Axis Brake: config_sr.h defines SR_E_BRAKE but tpic6b595.h says E has no brake (line 97). Verify with hardware. Currently reject BRAKE E commands.
